## **`palloc`**

### Description
The function allocates memory in physical pages. 
It is typically used by low-level system software to allocate contiguous blocks of physical memory.

### Parameters
| Name            | Type     | Description                                |
|-----------------|----------|-------------------------------------------|
| size            | uint64_t | The number of bytes to allocate           |
| align           | uintptr_t| Alignment requirement for returned address |

### Return Value
- A pointer to the allocated physical memory block.
- NULL if allocation fails.

### Usage Example 
```c
#include <stddef.h>
#define PAGE_SIZE 4096

// Allocate a page of memory aligned at PAGE_SIZE boundary
void *ptr = palloc(PAGE_SIZE, PAGE_SIZE);

if (!ptr) {
    // Handle allocation failure
}
```

### Importance Level
- Medium-High Impact  
- Caller Count: ~High (Called by various kernel components such as device drivers, memory managers)
